transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

I’m here because… since my wife had a fall, I haven’t really been myself. I used to be organized, the one with the lists and the plan. Now I sit at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart, and I either end up crying or snapping over nothing.

Things are piling up—bills, calls I’m supposed to make, the housework. I just… can’t seem to make myself function.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or activities?
I don’t know… I haven’t really thought about it that way. I’m not doing much of anything lately, but I can’t say if it’s because I’ve lost interest or just… everything feels hard.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough or blaming yourself for things that aren’t your fault?
I… I don’t know. I suppose I’ve wondered if I should be handling things better, but I can’t really say I’m blaming myself for things. Not sure.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, since your wife’s fall?

Most days, yes… I suppose that’s fair. Since her fall, I’ve just not been myself. I’ll sit there staring at her medication chart and end up crying, or I snap over some small thing. Everything piles up, and I can’t seem to get moving.
Would you say that you feel depressed most of the day, nearly every day, since your wife’s fall?

Yes… most of the day, most days. Since my wife’s fall, I’ve just… changed. I used to be the one with lists, with a plan. Now I sit at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart and end up crying, or I snap over nothing. Things are piling up—bills, calls, the house—and I can’t seem to make myself function.
Would you describe your mood as sad or depressed, rather than just feeling overwhelmed or stressed?

Yes… sad, I think. Not just stressed. Since my wife’s fall, I’ve gone from being the one with the lists and the plan to sitting at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart, crying… or snapping over nothing. And then the bills, the calls, the housework just pile up. I can’t seem to make myself function.
Have you noticed that you no longer take pleasure in activities or things you used to enjoy?
I… I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about it that way. Things just feel different lately, but I don’t know if I’d say that exactly.
Have you noticed any trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions lately?
I don’t know… I mean, I haven’t really paid attention to it that way. Some days I feel a bit muddled, but I couldn’t say for sure.
Have you found it hard to focus or think clearly, like when you’re trying to read or follow a conversation?
Maybe a little, but I’m not sure. I don’t really read much lately, and conversations… I suppose I drift sometimes. I haven’t kept track.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, activities, or even spending time with people?
I don’t really know. I mean… I haven’t been paying attention to whether I’m enjoying things or not. Things just feel a bit off, I suppose, but I can’t say more than that.
Have you found that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or activities, don’t bring you any pleasure anymore?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been doing much of those things lately, so it’s hard to tell if they don’t bring pleasure or if I’m just… not paying attention to it.
Have you noticed that you don’t get any enjoyment out of things that used to make you happy, like hobbies, activities, or even spending time with others?
I can’t really say. I haven’t been doing much, and when I’m with people I’m not exactly thinking about whether I’m enjoying it. It just… passes.
Have you noticed any significant difficulty thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions lately?
I’m not sure. I mean, I have moments where I’m a bit scattered, I suppose, but I haven’t really been keeping track of whether it’s significant or anything.
Would you say that you no longer feel pleasure or enjoyment in activities that used to make you happy, like hobbies or spending time with others?
I don’t know that I’d put it that strongly. I haven’t really been doing much of those things, so… I’m not sure what I’d be comparing it to.
Would you say that you don’t feel any pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, activities, or even time with friends?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really tested it, if that makes sense. I don’t do much of those things lately, so I can’t say whether there’s no pleasure there or I just haven’t been paying attention.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, activities, or spending time with others?
I don’t really know. I mean… maybe I’m doing less, but I can’t say clearly that I’ve lost interest. I haven’t paid enough attention to it.
Would you say that you don’t feel any pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, activities, or even time with friends?
I don’t know. I feel like I already said… I haven’t really been around much of that lately, so it’s hard for me to say one way or the other.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, activities, or spending time with others, even when you do them?
I can’t really say it’s completely gone. I haven’t noticed it in a clear way… I just don’t know.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, activities, or spending time with others, even when you do them?
I’m not sure I can answer it that strongly. “Completely” feels like more than I can say. I just… haven’t really noticed enough to be sure.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, activities, or spending time with others, even when you do them?
I don’t think I can say “completely.” I mean… maybe things feel different, but I haven’t really tested it much, so I don’t know.
